articles.title: Home Assistant makes checks for leaked secrets opt-in
articles.dek: Third-party checks stop by default, including on installations whose owners never changed the setting.
body: Home Assistant makes its check for compromised secrets a deliberate choice. Supervisor stops enabling the Have I Been Pwned check by default, including on existing installations whose owners never changed this security setting.

The service receives the first five characters of a secret’s SHA-1 fingerprint, rather than the secret itself. The change responds to concerns that even this limited information derived from a secret was sent to a third party without an explicit choice.
An explicitly saved setting keeps its existing value. Owners who want the check can enable it with ha security options --pwned=true.

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps smart playlists in step with music folders
articles.dek: A folder rule turns an existing file collection into a playlist that follows additions.
body: Music Assistant lets listeners build a smart playlist from selected music folders. Adding files to those folders updates the playlist, giving people who organize their collection on disk a way to keep that organization inside Music Assistant.

The rule editor browses the configured filesystem music sources and lets the listener select folders. Stefan Gerasch supplies the server and interface changes in his first contributions to both repositories, with review by Marvin Schenkel.

articles.title: Home Assistant filters activity by who or what caused it
articles.dek: Separate household actions from automations, scripts and outside integrations.
body: Home Assistant’s activity panel gains a Triggered by filter for tracing why something changed. It can show actions attributed to people, automations or scripts, or integrations such as HomeKit and Google Assistant.

The filter follows the cause already shown beneath each activity entry. Accounts without an associated person, such as an account used by Node-RED, count as integrations; entries with no known cause appear under Other.

pullRequests.title: Add a triggered by filter to the activity panel

articles.title: AnyList shopping lists join Home Assistant
articles.dek: Items, completion states and descriptions stay synchronized in both directions.
body: Home Assistant connects AnyList shopping lists to its to-do lists, with changes to item names, completion and descriptions synchronized in both directions. Live updates from AnyList keep the lists current without waiting for a periodic refresh.

Lists created, renamed or removed while Home Assistant is running are reflected too. This first connection covers shopping lists; recipes and meal planning are outside its scope. It relies on AnyList’s cloud service and the behavior of its web application, which has no public API.

articles.title: Home Assistant expands electricity-price planning in Belgium and New Zealand
articles.dek: ENGIE gains day-ahead prices, while ecosmart supplies spot prices and its forecast curve.
body: Home Assistant adds more information for shifting electricity use into cheaper periods. ENGIE Belgium households with dynamic tariffs gain hourly and quarter-hourly day-ahead price readings, while a new ecosmart connection brings New Zealand wholesale prices and forecasts into Home Assistant.

ENGIE reports the current and next price, today’s lowest and highest prices, and whether tomorrow’s prices have been published. Its public price endpoint needs no additional credentials; households without a dynamic tariff receive none of these new readings.

For ecosmart customers, the connection reports the current spot price including GST and the forecast for the current half-hour, with the published forward curve attached. Stale spot readings become unavailable instead of continuing to direct an automation with an old price. This first version supplies readings, not charging controls.

pullRequests.title: Add EPEX day-ahead prices to ENGIE Belgium

articles.title: Home Assistant stops forged identities reaching app sign-ins
articles.dek: Supervisor ensures apps receive only the identity of the signed-in household member.
body: Home Assistant closes a way for an authenticated user to pose as someone else inside apps that trust Supervisor’s sign-in information. Requests could supply differently capitalized identity headers that escaped the proxy’s filter and reached the app beside the genuine identity.

Supervisor checks those header names without regard to capitalization and supplies its own values after filtering. The protection covers both ordinary requests and live WebSocket connections; the reported impersonation risk concerns apps using these headers for single sign-on.

articles.title: Home Assistant prevents long requests from stalling Supervisor
articles.dek: A request filter stops spending minutes on specially shaped addresses.
body: Home Assistant’s Supervisor stops a long, carefully shaped request address from tying up its request-handling loop. The security filter runs before authentication, so the costly check could interrupt other work before the sender had signed in.

Manuel Rüger’s correction keeps the scan’s work proportional to the address length. Reported tests of 24 KB requests took 0.2 to 2.4 milliseconds rather than minutes; comparisons across 800,000 generated inputs found no change in what the filter blocked.

articles.title: Home Assistant reads eight SenseCAP sensor models over LoRaWAN
articles.dek: Measurements and battery readings extend the shared long-range wireless connection.
body: Home Assistant adds measurements and battery readings for SenseCAP models S2101 through S2107 and S2120 through its shared LoRaWAN connection. These eight supported models extend the recent network overview with readings that household dashboards and automations can use.

articles.title: Music Assistant finds YouTube Music tracks listed only as videos
articles.dek: An optional search setting includes video results alongside songs.
body: Music Assistant adds an Include videos in search results setting for YouTube Music. It finds tracks that the service lists only as videos and that song-only searches therefore missed.

The option starts off. When enabled, video and song results share the requested limit and duplicate entries are removed; radio and library imports keep their existing behavior. This is Joseph Petersen’s first contribution to Music Assistant’s server, reviewed by Marvin Schenkel.

pullRequests.title: Allow including videos in YouTube Music searches

articles.title: Assist presses named buttons from an English voice request
articles.dek: Commands such as “press the doorbell button” work with button entities and helpers.
body: Assist understands English requests to press a named Home Assistant button, including button helpers. Phrases such as “press the doorbell button,” “push doorbell” and “press reset counter” reach the existing button action.
Michael Hansen adds the English sentence patterns and a Pressed response. The change uses Home Assistant’s existing button action.

articles.title: Music Assistant changes how Yandex Music Connect chooses its account
articles.dek: Existing custom-credential or automatic-player setups need an explicit account and player selection.
body: Music Assistant’s Yandex Music Connect connection uses a linked Yandex Music account and a specifically selected player. Existing setups using their own credentials or automatic player selection need to be reconfigured to choose both.

The connection adds repeat, shuffle and queue navigation, and improves recovery after authentication or connection failures. The device name follows the chosen player; credentials are not copied between providers.

pullRequests.title: Update Yandex Music Connect to v4.3.13 with linked accounts, AudioSource lifecycle, and queue controls

articles.title: Home Assistant reaches newer Helty ventilation panels
articles.dek: A cloud connection serves panels that no longer accept the older local protocol.
body: Home Assistant adds fan controls for newer Helty Flow ventilation panels, which communicate through the manufacturer’s cloud instead of exposing the local connection used by older panels. The separate integration offers four speeds and boost, night and free-cooling presets.

Controls become unavailable when the cloud has no report from a panel within the preceding two hours. Older locally connected panels keep their existing integration; this first cloud connection supplies fan controls, with sensor support outside its scope.

articles.title: Home Assistant repairs Broadlink radio commands that did nothing
articles.dek: RM4 Pro learning failures stop appearing successful, and correctly captured commands can be replayed.
body: Home Assistant corrects Broadlink RM4 Pro radio-command learning that could report success while saving a command the receiver ignored. Captures that started in the middle of a radio pulse gain the necessary correction, alongside more reliable frequency and error handling.

Failed learning and sending actions report errors instead of a successful result, while commands captured before a later failure remain saved. The contributor verified that a newly learned command controlled a fixed-code patio heater on real RM4 Pro hardware.

roadmapUpdates.title: Replacing automation steps awaits approval
roadmapUpdates.summary: Niels’s proposal to replace a trigger, condition or action without rebuilding the row moves to Awaiting approval. Its revised rules preserve settings only when their field names match and their values remain valid, including trigger IDs used elsewhere in the automation.
